summary: The opt-in loopback host serves /preview/ for browser sign-in, read-only board discovery, refresh and logout. The page holds the bearer in memory and uses the existing Rust session and visibility operations. Both required Chromium journeys passed against disposable PostgreSQL schemas.
evidence: browser_reject_correct_list_logout: empty Enter stayed on the focused identifier. The unknown identifier advanced to the labelled, required masked field without a fetch. Change restored the identifier and cleared the password and alert. Unknown-account and wrong-password submissions showed the same rejection with password focus. A fresh connection found zero sessions before correction.

Correction produced one login POST, session resolution, then the list GET. The three visible, non-overlapping list rows matched the independently queried catalog positions, names and subscriptions: 203 Quartz, 202 Review, 201 Review. Hidden 204 was absent. PostgreSQL had one verifier linked to the fixture Viewer before creation of a separate same-account peer.

A fixture-local session-table lock made logout fail. Both session verifiers remained, and the window retained its rows and explicit Log out action. After release, the next click returned focus to the empty identifier with no visible protected controls or automatic login. Only the peer verifier remained and its client resolved. Membership, subscriptions and both Review boards' ordered items/revisions were unchanged.

browser_empty_unavailable_then_retry: removing membership and clicking Refresh showed No boards. Restoring membership and locking the fixture catalog past the host lock timeout yielded Retry board list with neither rows nor No boards. Releasing the lock made no automatic request; clicking Retry fetched the original three IDs in order. Fresh reads at empty, unavailable and recovery matched the same Viewer session, three subscriptions, expected membership, and 62 Outline/1 on 202 and 73 Sketch/1 above 61 Ink/1 on 201. After independent revocation, Refresh returned to sign-in.

Both browser cases passed serially using pointer and keyboard input, Chromium accessibility and layout observations, private automation pipes, and fresh temporary profiles. All 8 loopback_board_access cases, 23 locked workspace tests, the exact canonical-address case, and 13 serial Windows smoke cases passed. Workspace and Android formatting and git diff --check passed. The worker shell denied node --test scripts/run.test.mjs; runner regressions remain for coordinator verification. The opt-in clipboard and device journeys were not run.

Foreground command: cargo run --locked -p boardcraft-mobile-edit-host --features browser-smoke --example browser_board_preview. A follow-up Windows spot check reproduced a hidden fixture tab with focus on the body. With occluded-window backgrounding disabled for the foreground launcher, Chrome accepted input through the real masked form, displayed Quartz, Review, Review in stored ID order and reached the example's signed-in signal. Both unattended browser cases also passed.

Comparison is limited to the recorded existing-account rejection/correction, single-session logout and synthetic visibility/order contracts. No fresh reference browser comparison or lost-acknowledgment run was performed. Reload/session restoration, password reset, opening a board, history, full sidebar and mobile browser layout remain open.
